title: Edge Fallback SLA Assertion and Oncall Handover
summary: Pre-launch readiness huddle focused on edge fallback behavior, SLA assertion for 99/500ms targets, and formal oncall handover items after the upcoming canary. Identified three high-risk items: KV cache eviction skew, routing policy mismatch for low-latency tier, and telemetry gaps for fallback events.
action_items: Priya Sinha: Run kv-cache regression with 4k and 8k sequences, include perf histogram by 2026-09-17
Jordan Kim: Harden routing policy to prefer low-latency pool for dedicated customers, PR by 2026-09-14
Evan Ross: Add synthetic canary that triggers model-variant fallback, ship by 2026-09-13
Maya Patel: Update oncall runbook doc and add escalation matrix, draft by 2026-09-12
Tom Hsu: Prepare pager and mute thresholds for fallback bursts, confirm by 2026-09-15
next_steps: Run targeted kv-cache bench with the QA team and share spreadsheet link
Schedule a 30-min oncall walk-through next Thursday (inv sent)
Make quick rollback toggle available in the console for the canary
questions: What counts as a user-impacting fallback vs graceful degrade?
Do we have SLOs for model-variant fallback latency?
transcript:
Meeting Header: 
Date: 2026-09-10 
Start: 10:15 UTC 
Duration: 62 minutes 
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (PM); Evan Ross (Eng Lead); Priya Sinha (SRE); Jordan Kim (Infra); Maya Patel (Prod Ops); Sara Vega (Head of Release); Tom Hsu (Oncall); Ravi Malhotra (QA)

Auto Summary (auto): quick prelaunch check, focus on edge fallback semantics and oncall readiness.

00:00 Liam: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda — fallback semantics, sla assertion, oncall handover. We have 60ish minutes.
00:28 Evan: yeah, i'll kick off with the perf notes, we saw a regression in the kv cache when sequence spikes above 3k, it turns into this weird tail latency. not sure if it's scheduling or mem pressure.
00:52 Priya: mm-hmm, in my runs the k-v cash eviction looks off — i mean the k v cache tends to thrash when sequences pile up from batching. could be our prefix caching rules.
01:18 Jordan: i suspect a routing mismatch too, some requests for low-latency tier are going to the cost-optimized pool because of old policy id, i pushed a quick fix but we need canary.
01:45 Liam: right, we can't allow that for dedicated customers. our SLA target is 99% under 500ms for short-context queries, remember that.
02:12 Sara: from release side we need a clear rollback trigger, e.g. sustained 5-minute increase in 95th p50? p95? (laugh) sorry p95, or spikes in fallback rate.
02:42 Tom: for oncall — if fallback rate > 2% sustained for 10m, page the infra oncall, otherwise mute to paging and create an ops ticket. need to align thresholds.
03:05 Ravi: QA will run the smoke suite but we need an integration harness that can flip model variants to simulate fallback. Evan?
03:28 Evan: working on that, i've got a synthetic that toggles weights but it doesn't emit the fallback metric reliably, so the alerting won't trigger.
03:52 Maya: that's telemetry gap #1. we need explicit 'fallback_occurred' event with context (model_shim, route, tokens) so oncall can triage.
04:20 Priya: agreed — add that to instrumentation. also add KV cache eviction reason codes, otherwise it's opaque.
04:45 Jordan: scheduling wise — canary goes monday at 08:00 PDT, 2-hour ramp to 5% traffic, then 1 hour at 25% if green. we need the rollback toggle on the console by then.
05:10 Liam: risk register — kv-cache skew (high), routing policy mismatch (med), telemetry/alerts (med-high). any other unknowns?
05:33 Evan: quantization path differences could cause subtle perf delta on some kernels, but that's more model-level. will flag if it shows up.
05:58 Sara: security/compliance checks are green, audit logs working, though we should confirm KMS key rotation will not interrupt canary.
06:25 Jordan: KMS rotates tomorrow in staging, i'll coordinate so production keys untouched.
06:43 Tom: about the runbook — current steps assume fallbacks are rare; we need a short playbook for fallback storms: immediate mute, reduce canary traffic, enable fallback-debug logging, open incident channel.
07:15 Liam: write that down. Maya, can you own the runbook update?
07:26 Maya: yes i'll take it, will add explicit steps and a checklist.
07:40 Ravi: quick note — QA found intermittent 502s when we force-model-switch, maybe a race in the kv cache prime. i'll paste logs to the shared sheet.
08:05 Priya: that aligns with eviction thrash, the prime path is not atomic. need locking or sequence guard.
08:30 Evan: locking might add latency, we should try a compare-and-swap light guard first.
08:47 Liam: okay tradeoff: some complexity for stability vs slight p95 cost. Decision: prioritize stability for canary.
09:05 Sara: release windows: if we cut canary and hit rollback, we still want a 24h wait to reattempt. that's policy.
09:30 Tom: alert tuning — page on sustained errors, not on single spikes. set 10m window for p95 and fallback rate alerts.
09:55 Maya: i'll draft alert thresholds and share; also will add playbook steps in the doc.
10:20 Evan: for the synthetic canary toggles, i'll add a metric 'canary_fallback_count' and make sure it's emitted on every variant switch.
10:45 Priya: add eviction reason codes, and emit 'kv_eviction_reason' in telemetry.
11:10 Liam: good. next, SLA assertion test plan — Ravi?
11:28 Ravi: QA plan: run 10k synthetic short queries (<=128 tokens) at 200 RPS, measure p50/p95/p99; also run burst test to emulate client spikes. we'll share the spreadsheet.
11:55 Evan: include cold-start tests to capture kernel warmup. our perf histograms still have wide tails there.
12:20 Sara: we need runbook attachments in the release email, an ops checklist and rollback steps.
12:45 Tom: oncall handover: i'll be oncall for the canary window, with Priya as second. Escalation to Evan then Liam.
13:05 Liam: ok, recap and owners: Priya runs kv-cache regression, Jordan fixes routing PR, Evan adds canary metric, Maya updates runbook, Ravi runs QA harness.
13:30 Maya: i'll add due dates and invite the handover session.
13:50 Liam: any final questions? (pause) ok thank you, we'll reconvene after qa results.
14:10 END
file_notes: Transcript contains common transcription artifacts: 'kv cache' sometimes transcribed as 'k v cash' or 'k-v cash', 'canary' sometimes 'can-a-ry'. Speakers occasionally overlap; timestamps are approximate. References to console/toggle/link are shorthand (links in shared doc).
